sources.title: Google Earth Engine — Landsat Collection 1 to Collection 2 migration
facts: Collection 2 Level-2 reflectance uses the new scale and additive offset.
Collection 2 thermal bands use a distinct scale and additive offset.
Google provides an explicit example that scales SR and ST separately.

sources.title: Google Earth Engine — ee.Image.normalizedDifference
facts: If either input band has a negative pixel value, the output pixel from normalizedDifference() is masked.
Google recommends ee.Image.expression() when negative values must not be masked.

sources.title: Google Earth Engine — ee.Image.reduceRegion
facts: Google states it is good practice to explicitly define analysis scale (or crsTransform) and crs to avoid unexpected results from undesired defaults.

sources.title: Google Earth Engine — ee.Image.reduceRegions
facts: The API supports explicit scale, crs, and crsTransform for region analysis.

sources.title: Google Earth Engine Data Catalog — COPERNICUS/S1_GRD
facts: COPERNICUS/S1_GRD is provided in decibels after log scaling.
Raw power values are exposed separately through COPERNICUS/S1_GRD_FLOAT.

sources.title: Google Earth Engine Data Catalog — Harmonized Sentinel-2 MSI Level-1C
facts: QA60 historically contained rasterized cloud polygons.
Those polygons stopped being produced in 2022.
Legacy-consistent QA60 bands are constructed again from MSK_CLASSI beginning in February 2024.

sources.title: Google Earth Engine Data Catalog — Harmonized Sentinel-2 MSI Level-2A
facts: The QA60 discontinuity applies to the Level-2A harmonized collection.

v0.1.0 uses the conservative interior interval beginning 2022-01-26 and ending before 2024-02-28; the boundary dates themselves are intentionally not linted in v0.1.0 to avoid false positives from documentation-boundary ambiguity.
